messages:
ira: Heads-up: new candidate sampler (longtail-hardneg) in onboard pipeline dropped NDCG@10 on the tail_queries cohort, MRR roughly flat. curious if negative sampling skewed difficulty distribution.
michael: numbers? tail_queries = queries with 75th+ doc length or low-frequency intents?
ira: cohort definition: tail_queries_v1 (queries freq < 0.05% and avg doc tokens > 120). quick snapshot from yesterday: 
```
# cohort tail_queries_v1 (n=8k)
model baseline-sampler (fp16) -> MRR: 0.312, NDCG@10: 0.658
model longtail-hardneg (fp16) -> MRR: 0.309, NDCG@10: 0.621
%ndcg drop ~5.7% absolute, mrr ~1% relative
```
zoe: 5.7% NDCG absolute is large. curious why MRR stable but NDCG falls; maybe hardneg increases near-misses in top10 but not top1?
andrew: I ran a per-query histogram: hardneg increases the density of near-miss scores in ranks 5-10. example: q-9012 fp16 top10 scores: [0.81,0.64,0.63,0.58,0.55,0.52,0.49,0.45,0.43,0.40] vs hardneg: [0.81,0.80,0.78,0.76,0.74,0.72,0.70,0.65,0.60,0.55] -> ndcg drops because gold gets diluted among many high-scoring distractors, even if top1 preserved.
ira: is this a labeling issue? maybe the new sampler pulls candidates that are actually relevant but unlabeled (false negatives), which would artificially lower ndcg.
michael: good point. what's our unlabeled detection rate? run a small manual audit: sample 100 queries and label top10 candidates from hardneg run.
qa-bot: scheduled job 1865432110: manual-audit-100 (link: https://ci.redwood/review/1865432110).
(30m)
qa-bot: manual-audit results posted. summary: ~22% of high-scoring distractors were actually judged relevant by human auditors (unlabeled positives).
zoe: that explains NDCG drop — the metric penalizes placing those items below gold, but they are true positives we don't credit. MRR looks stable because it depends only on first correct hit which is usually the curated gold.
andrew: mitigation ideas: 1) clamp candidate sampler to avoid pulling from the same domain/host as gold when using hardneg 2) expand label coverage for tail cohorts (active labeling) 3) use adjusted metrics that account for potential unlabeled positives (precision@k with human-in-the-loop).
michael: we should also run an eval where we exclude suspicious unlabeled positives from the candidate pool to measure the pure model delta. run A/B: (A) longtail-hardneg with candidates filtered by label-coverage mask (B) baseline-sampler.
ira: kicking off A/B now, 8k-sample mini-cohort. eval command: `python -m eval.run --cohort tail_queries_v1 --sampler longtail-hardneg --filter labeled_mask.csv --model fp16 --metric ndcg,mrr`
eval-bot: queued jobs: 1865432120 (filtered-hardneg), 1865432130 (baseline). links: https://ci.redwood/evals/1865432100/tail-sampler-ab
(20m)
eval-bot: results:
- baseline-sampler -> NDCG@10 0.658, MRR 0.312
- hardneg (filtered to labeled-only) -> NDCG@10 0.651, MRR 0.308
=> gap narrows but still ~0.7% ndcg absolute.
zoe: remaining delta might be real: hardneg indeed increases near-miss density even among labeled negatives. but big chunk was labeling coverage.
andrew: actionables:
- (ira) revert longtail-hardneg as default for onboard tail cohort until we expand labels or add filters.
- (michael) create an active-label job to label top-scoring hardneg candidates for tail_queries (estimate ~30k labels).
- (zoe) add a 'suspected-unlabeled-positive' detector in eval that flags high-score unlabeled items for human review (heuristic: score > 0.7 and not in labelset).
- (andrew) update eval dashboard to show unlabeled-positive rate per cohort so product and ML can see if sampled candidates are under-labeled.
ira: temporal note: this only affected onboarding sampler; production serving unaffected. still, we should be careful because onboarding metrics inform model promotions.
qa-bot: created tracker issue https://tracker.redwood/ML-2198 (tail cohort label expansion) and CI check PR 1865432150 (flag unlabeled-positive-rate > 5% as warning).
michael: long-term: consider using pairwise evals or normalized metrics less sensitive to label sparsity. also add a step in sampler to prefer negatives from similar-length docs but different host to reduce accidental positives.
ira: thanks team. putting sampler change on hold and will coordinate label expansion. :white_check_mark:
